newsitem.title: USA: Dow snaps 4-day winning streak ahead of Sept jobs.
newsitem.headline: Dow snaps 4-day winning streak ahead of Sept jobs.

text.p: The Dow industrials paused in their record run, snapping a four-session winning streak on mild profit-taking and caution ahead of Friday's key September employment report.

"Stocks and bonds are waiting to see the employment report and that will set the tone for stocks for the next three weeks, along with earnings reports. Today, people are just positioning themselves," said Hugh Johnson of First Albany.
After surging 65 points over the past four trading days, the Dow slipped one to about 5933.
The blue chip index set back-to-back record closing highs on Tuesday and Wednesday.

The S&P 500 fell one to about 693 after scoring its third consecutive all-time high finish on Wednesday. The NYSE Composite was off fractionally to about 370 after Wednesday snaring its fifth straight record.
The tech-rich Nasdaq Composite slipped three to 1233 after rallying 15 points on Wednesday.
Losers outpaced winners 12-11 on active NYSE volume of about 385 million shares.
The long bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.84 percent.

Thursday's economic reports were neutral to constructive for bonds. Weekly jobless claims for the week ended September 28 totalled 340,000, unchanged from the prior week and in line with economists' forecasts. U.S. factory orders fell 1.9 percent in August, the steepest drop since January 1993.

But Wall Street's attention was focused on Friday's job report. Economists expect September payrolls to rise 166,000, a considerably tamer rate of growth than August's 250,000 increase and the more than 200,000 each month since May.
"We are not expecting a surprise and any surprise would hit the market hard," said Harry Laubscher of Tucker Anthony.

"We are well into overbought territory. But fund managers are quite bullish and optimistic about tomorrow's report and are extending maturities on Treasuries. They wouldn't do that if they had any qualms about tomorrow," said Laubscher, a market analyst at Tucker Anthony.

Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany, said, "Evidence, especially from the purchasing managers report, showed manufacturing employment was soft in September and that hints job growth in the order of 150,000-175,000. And, the upward pressure on wages that hurt the market last month will likely moderate."
Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co, noted that the American Stock Exchange's securities broker dealer index rose two to 425.04 after hitting a record high 426.10.

"That's one group that has not been able to record new bull market highs in the past four months and it's usually a good indicator of the health of the market. It made a magrinal new high and historically this index has had a tendancy to peak six months prior to when a bull market records its peak," he said. "We've wiped away the nagging divergance."
Among the index's components, Schwab rose one to 24-1/2.
A.G. Edwards slipped 3/8 to 29-3/4 after hitting a 52-week high of 30-3/4, and Merrill Lynch slipped 1/4 to 68-3/4.

Among special situations, tobacco shares fell after the Florida Supreme Court ruled that a class-action suit against the industry could proceed to a trial next spring. The state's highest court rejected a tobacco industry plea to scuttle the case. Defendants include Dow component Philip Morris, off 1-1/8 to 91-1/4, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings which fell 3/8 to 26-1/2, Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries, off 1/4 to 13-1/2 in U.S. trading, and Lorillard Tobacco, a unit of Loews Corp, up 1/4 to 79-1/2.
Monsanto rose 1-1/4 to 39-7/8. PaineWebber said it expected an upside surprise in its third-quarter earnings.

Among those warnings of earnings shortfalls, EIS International, a maker of phone call processing systems, tumbled 5-1/8 to 7-7/8, Peak Technologies slumped 9-7/8 to 11-7/8, and Wall Data shed 9-1/4 to 14.

Arbor Software lost 5-5/8 to 37-1/8 after news it sued Comshare, one of its distributors, alleging underpayment of royalties. Hambrecht & Quist said December and March quarter revenues at Arbor may fall as much at 25 percent from the loss of sales to Comshare. Comshare lost 2-1/4 to 13.
Wang Labs rose 2-1/8 to 22 after news it is in talks with Eastman Kodak about a possible deal involving Wang's software business. Kodak rose 1/2 to 78-1/2.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.02 to 1233.09.
The S&P 500 index fell 1.23 to 692.78.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
